thread:
marta_ops: Heads-up — planning a quiet-hour maintenance window this Thu 02:30-04:30 UTC for a thermal microcode update + rolling reboots in eu-west1. We'll stagger cordons to avoid host starvation. Affected pool: eu-west1-gpu-pool-1 (mixed a100/eia). Expect transient admissions/backfills; main goal is zero customer-visible failures. Cost note: backfilling into burst dedicated nodes will increase spend.

john_infra: ETA on the start and concurrency? can we cap simultaneous drains to 5% of capacity?

marta_ops: Start 2026-03-25T02:30Z. Window 2h. Plan: rolling batches of 8 nodes every ~15m, ~64 nodes total. Target no more than 5% concurrent running pods; will throttle eviction if pressure rises.

li_sre: Recommend a canary cohort first 02:30-02:45 in eu-west1-edge. We'll watch p99 token latency, admission rejection, and GPU queue depth. I'll add a probe that fires if admission_drop_rate > 0.5% for 5m.

chris_runtime: We also need KV/prefix cache priming before heavy traffic moves. Preseed plan:

```
redwoodctl cache seed --pool eu-west1-burst --prefixes /prompts/seedset-v3 --parallel 10
```

marta_ops: Pre-drain commands for node ops (will run via runbooks):

```
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```

john_infra: Cost question: If we backfill into the dedicated burst pool, rough delta +$2.5k/hr. Need finance signoff if total > $5k. Who owns that approval?

marta_ops: Finance cc @oncall_support. Worst-case estimate: 2h * $2.5k = $5k. If canary looks good we should be under that; will escalate if projection grows.

oncall_support: I'll open a status incident and draft customer-facing messaging. Send me bullets for the notice.

marta_ops: Draft messaging: "Planned maintenance in eu-west1 GPU pool. Rolling reboots and brief latency increases possible; no sustained downtime expected. Window: 02:30-04:30 UTC." Add link to status page once live.

li_sre: Dashboards/alerts to enable: p99 token latency, queue depth, admission drop rate, kv-cache-hit ratio, and synthetic workload against redwood-base-4x at 10 qps. I'll create temporary panels.

chris_runtime: Add an automatic fallback policy if p99 > 250ms for 5m: switch to model-compat-2 (quantized variant). Command for rollout:

```
redwoodctl rollout create --name maintenance-eu-west1 --strategy staggered --batch-size 8 --fallback model-compat-2
```

john_infra: Who is on-call for rollback/mitigation in case of systemic regression?

marta_ops: Incident lead: li_sre. Node ops: john_infra. Runtime/fallback monitoring: chris_runtime. Comms: me (marta_ops).

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: maintenance-eu-west1 at 2026-03-25T02:20Z. Canary job started.

oncall_support: Status page posted at 02:00Z and customers with Dedicated contracts notified. I'll keep the thread updated.

li_sre: Canary cohort draining started 02:30Z. Early signals: p99 latency +2ms, admission stable. No errors in 1st 10m.

marta_ops: Good. If p99 exceeds 120ms for 3 consecutive 3-min buckets we pause and investigate.

john_infra: Batch 2 kicking off 02:45Z. Pre-seed cache success on burst nodes. Observability shows a small, expected spike in egress/cpu — monitoring.

chris_runtime: Completed prefix priming for remaining prefixes. Fallback not triggered. Queue depth steady.

oncall_support: Finance confirmed contingency funds approved up to $7k for this window. Will notify if we cross thresholds.

li_sre: Batch 5 observed a flapping pod due to stale node label/toleration mismatch. Quick fix: removed stale toleration and resumed drain. No customer impact.

marta_ops: Closing window early at 04:10Z — all nodes returned to Ready and autoscaling normalized. We'll run a short smoke eval and then post a cost + impact summary tomorrow. Great work team :tada:

john_infra: Acknowledged. I'll add notes to the postmortem about label hygiene and improving preflight checks.

chris_runtime: I'll run QA evals against seeded prefixes and drop results in the maintenance board.

oncall_support: Status update closed and customers notified. Thanks everyone.
summary: quiet-hour rolling maintenance in eu-west1 with staggered drains, cache priming, canary cohort, cost contingency, and automatic fallback configured
